steps: Check whether the readiness failures started with a deploy. If a deploy is within 30 minutes of the first failure, roll it back before doing anything else.
Check payments-gw before restarting checkout-api. checkout-api times out when payments-gw saturates, and restarting checkout-api while payments-gw is the cause loses in-flight orders for nothing.
Restarting is safe only once the upstream is healthy. Scale rather than restart when the pods are up but slow.
Do not scale payments-gw above 6 replicas: the acquirer caps us at 240 connections in total and more replicas means more refused sockets, not fewer.

payments-gw.page: the payments on-call, always — this one holds money
steps: A saturated connection pool with the acquirer refusing sockets is the acquirer's cap, not ours. Scaling makes it worse.
Roll back the most recent config change to the pool before touching replicas.
If the acquirer is refusing at their cap, the only real lever is shedding load at checkout-api.
